criteria.quote: What if breaking your claws lasted just one day?
criteria.revision: Replace the generic hypothetical with: “Sandslash can snap off the claws and spikes it uses to attack—then they grow back tomorrow.” Hold back the regrowth line until the reveal if you want more suspense.

criteria.quote: Sandslash may snap off its spikes and claws digging too fast.
criteria.revision: Replace “Bad news for a Pokémon that attacks with both” with the concrete details: “Sandslash uses its sharp claws to slash and its spines to jab foes.”

criteria.quote: How can Sandslash keep fighting after losing its claws and spikes?
criteria.revision: Change the open loop to match what the research can answer: “If digging can break both its claws and spikes, how long does Sandslash have to live with the damage?” This points directly toward the one-day reveal without implying unsupported continued fighting.

criteria.quote: Bad news for a Pokémon that attacks with both.
criteria.revision: Make the middle beat deepen the conflict instead of restating it: “Its own digging can snap off the claws and spikes it relies on for slashing and jabbing.” Then delay the regrowth reveal until the following scene.

criteria.quote: The Pokédex says broken claws and spikes grow back in a day.
criteria.revision: The surprise is weakened because the title, premise, and first scene already reveal it. Retitle the story around the breakage—“Sandslash Can Snap Off Its Own Attack Tools”—and reveal “They grow back in a day” only after showing what the claws and spikes are used for.

criteria.quote: ITS WEAPONS JUST BROKE / THE DAMAGE DOESN’T LAST / SANDSLASH IS FINE AGAIN
criteria.revision: Give the beats distinct jobs: cause (“digging too fast can snap them”), function (“claws slash; spines jab”), reveal (“they grow back in a day”), and an additional concrete detail (“broken claws and horns can be used to carve plows”). Remove captions that merely repeat the regrowth.

criteria.quote: By the next day, Sandslash is not bothered by losing them.
criteria.revision: End with a fuller resolution: “Its own digging can break the claws and spikes it attacks with, but they grow back the next day—and the Pokédex says Sandslash is not bothered by the temporary loss.” This resolves both the cause and the opening concern.

criteria.quote: Smart recovery, or a terrible weakness?
criteria.revision: Replace the unsupported “terrible weakness” framing with: “Is a claw that returns tomorrow still a vulnerability today—or does one-day regrowth make the breakage irrelevant?” Both sides are grounded in the stated temporary loss and next-day recovery.
